intuition.title: Why combine these colloids?
intuition.text: The authors pursued binary order as a route to controlled placement and stoichiometry in future nanocrystalline solids. They cite Ag⁺ as a p-type dopant in bulk PbTe; the assembly itself does not prove atomic doping.

intuition.title: Why tune sizes and ligands?
intuition.text: The authors identify relative size and monodispersity as factors for ordered assembly. They add charged amphiphilic ligand in some preparations to narrow charge-state spread, but did not independently verify the charge distributions or assign each Figure 3 specimen to a specific additive branch.

scopeLabel: Main-text binary assembly method and Figure 3 only; PbTe precursor preparation belongs to ref. 17. SI and films excluded.

sourceAudit.scope: The saved audit_sha256 identifies the earlier scoped quick audit, not the targeted U1/U2 review. Independent targeted review accepted the Figure 3 input-colloid sizes and the reported solvent/modifier alternatives only. SI Figure S1 was checked only to exclude an unproven Figure 3 aliquot join; the SI as a whole and cited ref. 17 remain unreviewed. Neither Figure 3 specimen is assigned a particular solvent, modifier, or Figure 2 aging aliquot. Release remains pending.

general_background.title: Thermodynamics and kinetics
general_background.summary: Thermodynamics describes which states are energetically favoured, while kinetics governs how quickly a system can move between them. A change can be favourable yet proceed slowly when an activation barrier or limited transport restricts the pathway.
